content: The National Health Workforce Accounts Implementation Guide is a document published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2018. It provides a framework for countries to systematically collect, monitor, and use data on their health workforce to achieve universal health coverage, the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, and other national and global health objectives. The guide is designed to support the implementation of the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030. The guide emphasizes the importance of robust data collection and analysis of health labor markets using harmonized metrics and methodologies. It outlines a system called the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA), which enables countries to progressively improve the availability, quality, and use of health workforce data. This system is intended to provide a comprehensive overview of the dynamics of the health workforce, including information on workforce density, education, financing, and migration. The NHWA framework is structured around a labor market analysis approach and includes key indicators that are detailed in the WHO NHWA Handbook. A web platform has also been developed to help countries store data, monitor indicators, and report national health workforce statistics to WHO. The implementation of NHWA involves eight steps organized into three phases: conceptualization, operationalization, and process revision and sustainability. These steps include obtaining governmental buy-in, establishing governance structures, scoping and planning, developing a legal framework, compiling and analyzing data, validating data, disseminating findings, and revising processes as needed. The guide stresses that these steps should be adapted to each country's specific context and existing health information systems. The guide is primarily intended for policymakers, program managers, and officials involved in health workforce policy and strategy, as well as researchers and organizations monitoring health workforce data. It provides recommendations for integrating data sources within broader health reporting frameworks and offers insights into the impact of health workforce capacity on health system delivery and efficiency. The NHWA framework does not replace existing systems for monitoring and reporting health data but complements them. It encourages collaboration among stakeholders to define responsibilities within a national structure and ensures that activities to strengthen health workforce data are systematic and aligned with existing health information systems. The guide also outlines the roles of various entities involved in NHWA implementation, including a focal point within the Ministry of Health, a multistakeholder coordination working group, and a secretariat responsible for coordination and administration. Regular reviews of the NHWA processes are recommended to ensure efficiency, effectiveness, and alignment with national laws and governance considerations.
